item.title: APEC: Striving Together for Shared Prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Twelve years ago, Chinese President Xi Jinping invoked the image of swan geese, calling on APEC economies to enhance cooperation and embark on a new flight. Today, across the vast Pacific, the APEC family sails together toward shared prosperity and a brighter future.

item.title: Xi says advancing China-Mexico ties significant to Global South in seeking strength through unity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that advancing China-Mexico relations to new heights, across broader areas and in greater depth is of great significance to implementing their respective national development strategies and supporting the Global South in seeking strength through unity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. China is ready to work with Mexico to steer bilateral relations toward high-quality development, promote the building of an Asia Pacific that is prosperous, stable, open, interconnected, universally beneficial, inclusive, united and mutually supportive, as well as a more just and equitable global governance system, and contribute to world peace and common development, Xi added. Xi called on China and Mexico to deepen political mutual trust, strengthen exchanges and cooperation at all levels, stay committed to mutual benefit and win-win results, strengthen strategic alignment, and deepen cooperation on infrastructure, science and technology, clean energy, culture and tourism. He stressed the need for both sides to uphold fairness and justice, boost multilateral cooperation, enhance coordination at multilateral platforms such as the United Nations, and safeguard the basic norms governing international relations. Xi also called for deepening cooperation between China and Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries by advancing the five programs for the China-LAC community with a shared future. Noting that Mexico and China enjoy deep-rooted friendship, share similar development philosophies and have witnessed fruitful cooperation across various fields, Sheinbaum said Mexico is ready to expand cooperation with China in areas such as trade, investment, science and technology, manufacturing and artificial intelligence, while promoting exchanges in health, education, culture and tourism. She said China, as this year's APEC host, has played an important role in advancing Asia-Pacific cooperation, expressing confidence that the upcoming APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting would be a complete success and lay a solid foundation for future regional cooperation. Mexico stands ready to work with China to strengthen multilateral coordination, uphold multilateralism, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, said Sheinbaum. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)

item.title: Xi says China ready to further develop ties with Peru
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday said China is ready to work with Peru to elevate the comprehensive strategic partnership between the two countries to new heights and deliver greater benefits to the two peoples. China has remained Peru's largest trading partner and largest export destination country for 12 consecutive years, Xi said while meeting with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Fujimori is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Xi also noted that the protocol upgrading the China-Peru free trade agreement (FTA) took effect officially about two weeks ago, and the Chancay Port, built with the participation of Chinese enterprises, has given a strong boost to economic and trade cooperation between Asia and Latin America. Xi called for closer exchanges between the two countries' governments, legislative bodies, political parties, and localities to strengthen political mutual trust. He also urged both sides to make full use of the protocol upgrading the FTA, consolidate traditional cooperation in infrastructure, energy and resources, and explore potential in emerging fields such as new energy and artificial intelligence. He called for enhancing cooperation in culture, education, tourism, archaeology and health to carry forward the traditional friendship. Xi also said the two sides should strengthen communication and coordination within the United Nations, APEC and other frameworks to uphold true multilateralism and free trade, and safeguard international fairness and justice. Fujimori said Peru firmly adheres to the one-China principle, stands ready to strengthen high-level exchanges, and will use the protocol upgrading the FTA as an opportunity to enhance people-to-people exchanges and promote cooperation in trade, investment and infrastructure. Peru welcomes further investment by Chinese companies and will provide an open and stable business environment, she said, noting that projects such as the Chancay Port have played an important role in Peru's economic development. Fujimori also called for closer people-to-people and party-to-party exchanges, and thanked China for its support to Peru in addressing El Nino challenges. Peru is willing to strengthen multilateral coordination with China and enhance friendship between the two peoples, she said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)

item.title: Xi calls for joint efforts to develop China-Chile ties
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Shen Hong) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that he is ready to work with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast to strengthen strategic guidance, keep to the right direction, and jointly draw a blueprint for the growth of bilateral relations, so as to support the development and prosperity of the two countries. Xi made the remarks during his meeting with Kast in Shenzhen. The Chilean president is in the southern Chinese city to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that Chile was the first South American country to establish diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, Xi said the bilateral ties had withstood the test of a changing international landscape and maintained sound and steady development for a long time. The most valuable experience is that the two sides respect each other, treat each other as equals, and pursue win-win outcomes, he said. As this year marks the 10th anniversary of the establishment of the China-Chile comprehensive strategic partnership and the 20th anniversary of the entry into force of the China-Chile Free Trade Agreement, the bilateral relations have reached an important juncture for building on past achievements and forging ahead into the future, Xi said. Xi noted that China and Chile should continue to support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests and major concerns, strengthen exchanges across multiple sectors and at various levels, and share experience in state governance. Given the complementarity of their economies and the solid foundation of their cooperation, the two countries should better align their development strategies through high-quality Belt and Road cooperation, promote traditional cooperation in trade, energy, minerals, infrastructure and astronomic research, and expand into emerging fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), polar scientific expeditions, and deep-sea exploration, Xi said. He stressed that China stands ready to enhance communication and coordination with Chile within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, jointly uphold true multilateralism, and act as defenders of the common interests of developing countries. China is willing to work with Latin American and Caribbean (LAC) countries to inject greater certainty into peace and development in the region, and push forward China-LAC cooperation, Xi said. Kast stated that since the establishment of diplomatic relations between Chile and China, their bilateral ties have developed steadily, regardless of changes in the international landscape. For many years, China has remained Chile's largest trading partner and the leading destination for its agricultural and mineral exports. Cooperation with China has provided important opportunities for Chile's economic and social development, and strengthening ties with China represents a consensus across all sectors of Chilean society, the president added. Chile will unswervingly adhere to the one-China policy, deepen its good relations with China, expand the scale of trade and investment cooperation, broaden collaboration in agriculture, mining, new energy vehicles, infrastructure development and AI, and promote exchanges in education and culture, Kast noted. Chile stands ready to strengthen coordination with China within multilateral frameworks such as APEC, uphold multilateralism, remain committed to free trade, and promote peace and development worldwide, he said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Chilean President Jose Antonio Kast, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Yan Yan)

item.title: APEC CEO Summit 2026 kicks off in Shenzhen with focus on regional cooperation, future prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit 2026 opened Tuesday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, bringing together business and political leaders from across the Asia-Pacific and beyond to discuss regional economic cooperation and future development. Under the theme "To Prosper and Win the Future Together," the two-day event has attracted more than 2,000 representatives from 21 APEC economies and 13 non-APEC economies, including Britain, France, Germany and Switzerland. Participants include representatives from 115 Fortune Global 500 companies, as well as heads of several international organizations and representatives of business associations from Russia, the United States and other economies. U.S. companies make up the largest group among participating companies from economies other than China, accounting for nearly 20 percent of the total. As an important part of the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week, the summit is expected to launch a Shenzhen initiative this year, marking the first time in the summit's 30-year history that an outcome document will be issued in the form of an initiative. In his welcome address, Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade and chair of the APEC CEO Summit 2026, expressed the hope that the dialogue will spark new ideas and forge broad consensus, injecting fresh momentum into the Asia-Pacific community and global growth. Attendees at the summit are discussing the new landscape of the Asia-Pacific economy and opportunities for cooperation. Key topics include crafting a new blueprint for connectivity, building an open and inclusive AI innovation ecosystem, and setting a new paradigm for sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific. Other sessions will focus on advancing the Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, exploring new paths for digital economy cooperation, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area and Asia-Pacific development opportunities, and promoting synergized digital and green transformation. An important event in the APEC calendar, the APEC CEO Summit has been held annually since 1996, serving as the highest-level platform for APEC economy leaders and business representatives to discuss open cooperation and advance regional economic development. As the host of APEC in 2026, China will hold the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen from Nov. 18 to 19. This year's gathering, under the theme "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together," will focus on three priority areas identified by China -- openness, innovation, and cooperation. These priorities are "particularly relevant today," according to Antonio Basilio, director of the secretariat of the APEC Business Advisory Council, a mechanism that allows the regional business community to participate in APEC cooperation and submit policy recommendations to APEC economy leaders. Basilio expects all sides to hold constructive dialogues during the APEC meeting, and enable businesses to conduct trade and investment activities under more coherent, transparent and predictable rules. Working together with other APEC member economies, China has hosted more than 300 APEC meetings and events this year, drawing a cumulative attendance of over 10,000 participants. In the economic and trade field, China and other APEC economies have reached nearly 50 practical outcomes. ■

item.title: Xi says improvement, development of China-Canada relations right choice
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that the improvement and development of China-Canada relations is a right choice that serves the interests of both peoples and is conducive to world peace, stability, development and prosperity. Xi made the remarks while meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Carney is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. The development of China-Canada relations over the years has shown that mutual respect, equality and mutual benefit, and seeking common ground while respecting differences are essential, Xi said. China stands ready to work with Canada to further advance their new strategic partnership, he added. Xi said China and Canada should build on the current momentum to enhance political mutual trust and steadily build the right perception of each other's development path and policy intent, deepen understanding of and respect for each other's core interests and major concerns, and properly manage and settle differences and disagreements. The two countries should better align efforts to deepen cooperation in traditional areas such as trade, energy, agriculture and finance, and expand cooperation in emerging areas including the green economy, e-commerce and the digital economy, in order to better harness each other's strengths and achieve win-win outcomes, he said. He called for deeper people-to-people exchanges and more exchanges and cooperation in education, culture, tourism, science, technology and youth as well as at subnational levels. He also proposed closer coordination to jointly practice true multilateralism, uphold the authority of the United Nations and the multilateral trading system, and build a more just and equitable global governance system. Carney said that bilateral relations have been on the right track of development since the launch of the Canada-China new strategic partnership during his meeting with Xi early this year. The two countries can fully advance and deepen cooperation on the basis of mutual respect, Carney said. Canada will work with China to pursue stronger cooperation in trade, investment, new energy, agricultural products, artificial intelligence, tourism and other areas, reduce the list of irritants, and expand the list of cooperation, he said. Canada stands ready to strengthen coordination with China to advance cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, uphold multilateralism, promote free trade, and contribute to stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region and the world, Carney added. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin)

item.title: Xi says to boost China-Papua New Guinea ties to new heights
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Papua New Guinean Prime Minister James Marape, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said Tuesday that China is willing to work with Papua New Guinea (PNG) to enhance political mutual trust and strengthen people-to-people and cultural exchanges, advancing the development of bilateral relations to new heights. China has always regarded PNG as a trustworthy good friend and good partner, Xi said while meeting with PNG Prime Minister James Marape in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Marape is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. Noting that the PNG government adheres to the one-China principle and takes concrete actions to support China's efforts to safeguard territorial integrity and national reunification, Xi said it is a just act in keeping with the trend of history. Xi stressed that China stands ready to work with PNG to strengthen exchanges on governance and development experience, better synergize high-quality Belt and Road cooperation and PNG's Connect PNG Program and other strategies, and deepen cooperation in trade and investment, infrastructure, agriculture and fisheries, and energy and minerals. China is also ready to explore new avenues of cooperation in the digital economy, financial services, green energy, science and technology to help PNG achieve sustainable development, Xi said. The two sides should strengthen coordination within multilateral fora such as the United Nations and the APEC, uphold international fairness and justice, expand cooperation in tackling climate change and protecting the marine environment, and safeguard the common interests of the Global South, Xi noted. China is a good friend and the most important partner of PNG, Marape said. Over the past 50 years of diplomatic ties, PNG has consistently adhered to the one-China principle, firmly supported China in safeguarding national sovereignty and territorial integrity, and resolutely backed China's efforts to achieve national reunification and advance national rejuvenation. PNG highly appreciates China's important role in guiding international affairs, supports the four global initiatives put forward by President Xi Jinping, and stands ready to strengthen multilateral coordination with China to jointly build an Asia-Pacific community, and promote prosperity and stability in the Asia-Pacific region, he said. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Papua New Guinean Prime Minister James Marape, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin)

item.title: Xi says China-Vietnam top-level exchanges inject positive energy into regional peace, development
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Bin) SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Tuesday met with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam in Shenzhen. In recent years, the top leaders of the two parties and the two countries have maintained close exchanges and reached important consensus on building a higher-level China-Vietnam community with a shared future that carries strategic significance, Xi said. This has helped advance bilateral relations and injected positive energy into regional peace and development, Xi added. The Vietnamese leader is in Shenzhen to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, scheduled for Nov. 18-19. During the meeting, Xi expressed willingness to deepen experience sharing with Vietnam, firmly support each other, and strengthen exchanges on self-supervision and self-governance of the parties, so as to ensure continuous progress in both countries' socialist causes and national development. "As comrades and brothers, China and Vietnam must stand together and weather the storms," Xi said. Xi also underscored the importance of enhancing mutual trust and solidarity, deepening all-round cooperation, jointly safeguarding peace and stability, and advancing shared development and prosperity. The two sides should properly manage maritime differences and steadily advance maritime cooperation, Xi said. Xi called on China and Vietnam to strengthen coordination within frameworks such as the United Nations, China-ASEAN cooperation and Lancang-Mekong cooperation, and to fulfill their duties as successive hosts of APEC in 2026 and 2027, respectively. Noting that the Vietnamese side views China as its most important strategic support, Lam said that, amid the current complex international situation, his country stands ready to strengthen solidarity and cooperation with China to support the development of both countries. Lam also pledged to work with China to safeguard maritime stability. As the next APEC host, Vietnam will build on the outcomes of APEC "China Year" and continue efforts to advance Asia-Pacific cooperation, the Vietnamese leader added. ■ General Secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam Central Committee and Vietnamese President To Lam, who is in China to attend the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Liu Weibing)

item.title: China's APEC journey witnesses quarter-century pursuit of shared prosperity with wider world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-17
SHENZHEN, Nov. 17 (Xinhua) -- Travelers arriving at Shenzhen's international airport this week are greeted by a message on screens: "Gather in Shenzhen. Witness the wonders." Among the visitors are leaders and business executives attending Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) events. They are gathering in a metropolis that many longtime residents still remember as little more than a sleepy town amid rice paddies and oyster beds. Nearly half a century after China launched reform and opening up, the changes set in motion have produced one of the world's most remarkable economic stories. Shenzhen is among its most striking chapters. And the miracle -- in the city and across China -- is still unfolding. Shenzhen's rise began in 1980, when China made the small town next to Hong Kong a testing ground for economic reform. More flexible policies opened the door to investment from overseas. Local businesses began producing for international markets, while foreign goods, production techniques and management expertise flowed in. The experiment proved successful. One indication came in 1991, when China joined APEC -- a milestone that highlighted how much the country and the wider world had to offer each other. The Shenzhen meeting, scheduled for Wednesday and Thursday, will mark the third time China has hosted the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting, following the one held in Shanghai in 2001 and the other in Beijing in 2014. Over the past quarter-century, China has evolved from an emerging economy striving to integrate into the global system to an economic powerhouse and a major engine of growth. Its rise has helped create prosperity well beyond its borders. OPENING UP China's confidence in openness rests largely on its own experience. Shanghai, China's first APEC host city, offers two contrasting chapters in that history. The Western-style banks and trading houses along the Bund testify to the city's early commercial prosperity. But they also recall a time when China found itself in an unequal position in the international order. The city was forced open to foreign trade in the 1840s, after China's defeat in the Opium War. The conflict reflected how prolonged seclusion could leave a country vulnerable in a rapidly changing world. After a series of military defeats and diplomatic setbacks, the Qing court was compelled in 1901 to sign a protocol with 11 imperialist powers. It imposed a heavy indemnity and granted foreign powers further privileges in China. A full century later, China was engaging with the world on a very different footing. In 2001, Shanghai welcomed leaders of APEC economies to discuss trade, investment and economic cooperation. By then, the People's Republic was more than half a century old, with a stronger economy and more developed institutions. There was plenty to fuel optimism that autumn. China had just won the bid to host the 2008 Olympics, and talks on its accession to the World Trade Organization (WTO) had concluded. More than two decades of reform and opening up had reshaped the country and raised expectations for its future, both at home and abroad. The photograph of Asia-Pacific leaders in traditional silk jackets became a defining image of the Shanghai gathering. China joined the WTO that December. Liu Chenyang, director of the APEC Study Center of Nankai University in Tianjin, said China's APEC membership had helped pave the way for this step. APEC's flexible, gradual approach to cooperation and emphasis on voluntary action made it easier for the country to align its economic practices with international norms. The country's accession to the WTO gave domestic companies broader and more predictable access to overseas markets. It also exposed China's own market to greater international competition. In the years that followed, China became widely known as the "world's factory." From clothing and furniture to electronics, affordable goods made in the country found their way into homes around the world. Multinational companies reconfigured their production networks, more foreign investment poured in, and trade flourished. For many Chinese families, these changes brought more job opportunities in cities, higher incomes, modern conveniences and better education for their children. As economic globalization gathered pace, China benefited from overseas orders, investment and technological know-how. In turn, it offered the world a vast and highly capable manufacturing base and, increasingly, a fast-growing consumer market. From 2001 to 2025, China's overall tariff level fell from 15.3 percent to 7.3 percent, a reduction that went well beyond its initial WTO accession commitments. By the end of the first quarter of this year, the cumulative stock of foreign direct investment in China exceeded 4 trillion U.S. dollars, roughly ten times the figure in 2001, data show. Foreign investors have continued to benefit from their presence in China. Returns on direct investment have run at around 9 percent in recent years, among the highest in the world. In the first five months of 2026, foreign-invested companies reinvested 35 percent more of their earnings in China than in the same period a year earlier. "China has been a great leader in the opening-up process," said Eduardo Pedrosa, executive director of the APEC Secretariat. A NEW ERA When APEC returned to China in 2014, the country's growing economic weight was already changing its relationship with the rest of the world. The country welcoming leaders to the picturesque outskirts of Beijing was the world's second-largest economy and largest manufacturer. Yet the global recovery from the financial crisis remained uneven, regional conflicts had flared anew, and protectionism and unilateralism continued to cast a shadow over the international economic order. China's development mattered far beyond its borders. He Xilin, an assistant research fellow at the China Institute of International Studies, said the 2014 APEC meeting marked China's rise as an influential participant in regional cooperation, when the country began to play a more active role in shaping its agenda and advancing cooperation. The Belt and Road Initiative, proposed in 2013, and the steps taken toward establishing the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank in 2014 reflected that shift. At the Beijing meeting, China pledged 40 billion dollars to help establish the Silk Road Fund, an initiative designed to improve connectivity. The problems these initiatives sought to address were familiar to China. Better roads meant lower costs for farmers bringing their produce to market. Reliable electricity kept factories running. More efficient ports helped businesses reach overseas customers and compete for orders. China had built such infrastructure on a vast scale. It was now seeking to share its experience with other countries. The APEC meeting in Beijing was held under the theme "Shaping the Future through Asia-Pacific Partnership." It formulated a roadmap for a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific, a vision first put forward in 2006, as well as the APEC connectivity blueprint for 2015-2025. China's vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity gave the country's expanding international role a broader purpose, grounded in common interests and mutual support. It envisages an open, inclusive, clean, and beautiful world of lasting peace, universal security, and common prosperity. Change was also underway at home. One year before the 2014 APEC meeting, China embarked on an unprecedented reform drive that reached deep into the economy and society, covering everything from industry and finance to public services, social welfare and environmental protection, in a bid to further unleash market potential. Ahead of the meeting, authorities temporarily shut down heavily polluting businesses in and around Beijing to improve air quality. The unusually clear skies were dubbed "APEC blue." Chinese leaders pledged to make such blue skies a lasting feature. More than a decade later, clear skies have become more commonplace, reflecting sustained efforts to curb pollution, upgrade the industrial structure and transform the energy mix. China ratified the Paris Agreement on climate change in 2016. Today, the country supplies about 70 percent of the world's solar modules and 60 percent of its wind power equipment. It has also recorded the largest and fastest increase in forest area worldwide. In September 2025, China announced its climate commitments for 2035, pledging to cut economy-wide net greenhouse gas emissions by 7 to 10 percent from peak levels, raise the share of non-fossil fuels in energy consumption to more than 30 percent, and bring total installed wind and solar capacity to 3,600 gigawatts. The year 2014 was a pivotal year in China's poverty-alleviation campaign, following the introduction of a targeted strategy in November 2013. The nationwide campaign lifted nearly 100 million rural residents out of poverty by 2021, eradicating absolute poverty in a country of 1.4 billion people. China thereby met the relevant target under the United Nations 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development a decade ahead of schedule. The experience highlights several factors relevant to fellow developing countries: economic growth is essential for poverty reduction; investment in physical assets must go hand in hand with investment in people; and targeted policies can deliver better results than the even distribution of resources. SHAPING THE FUTURE The choice of Shenzhen as the 2026 host offers a glimpse of how China is pursuing its next stage of development. Here, everyday life shows how innovation, openness and cooperation reshape the economy and create opportunities for others. Over decades of manufacturing for markets at home and abroad, Shenzhen has built a tightly knit ecosystem that brings together component suppliers, engineers, mold makers and logistics firms. Designs can be turned into prototypes in a matter of days, with materials and parts readily available nearby. The result is an unusually short path from concept to finished product. Shenzhen-based Huawei, Tencent, DJI and BYD grew out of this environment, illustrating how such an ecosystem can nurture globally competitive companies. China now leads the world in producing more than 200 major industrial products and has built the largest and most comprehensive manufacturing system. On factory floors, artificial intelligence is now changing manufacturing itself. In a lithium battery workshop in Shenzhen's Bao'an District, an AI-powered system monitors production and automatically adjusts robotic arms to meet the industry's precision standards, eliminating the need to halt production for manual adjustments. Such applications improve routine factory operations. But faster quotations, more precise production planning and fewer errors can also determine whether a company wins its next order. Today, Chinese companies increasingly supply energy storage equipment, new energy vehicles, industrial automation systems and digital solutions overseas. Such exports often involve technical training and expertise in organizing production and building supply chains. Beyond selling cars and building a factory in Cambodia, BYD provides training materials and instructors to help local educational institutions train more technicians. China once benefited from the technology and expertise brought by foreign investment. Its companies now help other countries build their own production capabilities. Such ties extend beyond trade in goods, linking Chinese businesses' growth more closely with local development. These developments are unfolding against a challenging global backdrop. Weak global growth has widened development gaps and heightened security risks. Rapid technological change is opening new opportunities while raising questions over ethics, security and the rules needed to govern its use. China is seeking to do more to help address these challenges. In May, it implemented zero-tariff treatment for imports from 53 African countries, easing market access for their goods. In July, representatives of 29 countries signed an agreement in Shanghai to establish the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. From trade and technology to climate change and regional security, China's choices increasingly carry global implications. The Shenzhen APEC meeting comes at a time when China's ties with the Asia-Pacific are closer than ever. As the largest trading partner of 13 APEC economies, China counts eight APEC members among its top 10 trading partners. It also accounts for more than 60 percent of the region's economic growth, underscoring its growing importance to the Asia-Pacific's economic future. From Shanghai to Beijing to Shenzhen, researchers have observed a pattern in China's hosting of APEC meetings: when consensus begins to fray, such meetings hosted by China often help bring economies back together. As this year's host, China is looking to build on those ties and give regional cooperation fresh impetus. The Shenzhen meeting is expected to push forward the free trade agenda, draw on China's strengths in the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and help Asia-Pacific economies navigate technological transformation. One key item on the agenda is closer coordination between the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership and the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership. Regional connectivity will also feature prominently, with leaders looking to build on work carried out under the APEC Connectivity Blueprint for 2015-2025. In 2019, Shenzhen was designated by the central authorities as a "pilot demonstration area of socialism with Chinese characteristics" to develop replicable reforms for other regions in China. China has set its own timetable: to basically achieve socialist modernization by 2035 and become a great modern socialist country in all respects by mid-century. Achieving these goals will further unlock China's economic potential and create more opportunities for countries around the world. More than two decades after China first hosted APEC, the spotlight is returning to China. The world is looking for greater synergy to power the Asia-Pacific and beyond, translating the vision of shared prosperity into tangible progress. ■
